newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares ease as foreigners mull return.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares ease as foreigners mull return.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.5 percent on Wednesday and market participants said the gradual decline was likely to continue because of the uncertainty surrounding the return of foreign investors.
The SBI index eased 6.91 points to 1,378.78. Overall 12 shares fell, four rose and 10 were untraded.
"Shares will continue declining slowly until banks open the first custodian accounts (for foreign investors), which may happen as early as next week," said one trader.

The Bank of Slovenia last month said that foreigners were required to open custodian accounts opened at a local bank if they wanted to trade in Slovenian securities. Since the announcement, the blue chip SBI index has shed 16.7 percent.

"The costs of these accounts remain unclear therefore it is hard to preduct whether these extra costs may reduce foreign interest in Slovenian shares," the trader said, adding that prices could jump as soon as foreigners returned to the market.
Banks said the cost of keeping the new accounts was likely to be about 12 percent of the amount handled.
Bank SKB was most actively traded, closing 1.12 percent lower at 57,200 on volume of 1,253 shares.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, down 10.28 percent to 13,000 on volume of 22 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, rising 10 percent to 14,300 on volume of two shares.
